_comment: The hellfire faction's production building, authored from nothing.
Scale and budget are taken from MEASURED retail peers, not chosen: the GLA barracks is
110 x 51 x 88 world units at 565 triangles, the war factory 100 x 58 x 122 at 684. A
building noticeably outside that envelope is either invisible at normal camera height or
swallows the units it builds, and neither failure names itself.
Coordinates are Z-UP, in the same frame the W3D ends up in. Ground is z = 0, so a part's
'at' is the CENTRE of its box and its size/2 is how far it reaches below that. Getting
this wrong buries the building or floats it, and both look like a scale bug rather than a
Part names are load-bearing. Each becomes a W3D sub-object, which is how an INI Draw
module shows or hides a piece and how the engine finds something to rotate.
name: HELLWORKS

parts._: Battered plinth. taper < 1 narrows the TOP, so the walls lean inward like poured
parts.__: concrete — the cheapest cue that reads as mass rather than as a floating box.
parts.name: PLINTH

parts._: Main hall, with the bay door cut straight through the -Y face. A boolean is the
parts.__: whole reason this pipeline goes through Blender: an opening is not expressible as
parts.___: a primitive, and faking it with a dark texture panel is what it replaces.
parts.name: HALL

parts._: Overhanging cap. Wider than the hall on purpose: the shadow line under an eave is
parts.__: what separates a roof from a lid.
parts.name: ROOF

parts._: Three stacks from ONE part via array — count and offset, not three copy-pasted
parts.__: blocks. 8 segments because at this camera distance a rounder cylinder spends
parts.___: triangles nobody can see, against a 169-triangle retail median.
parts.name: STACKS

parts._: Cooling louvres, arrayed up the flank and mirrored across X so both sides match
parts.name: LOUVRES
